To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
maternal and child malnutrition, including both undernutrition and overweight, is an important cause of child mortality and morbidity, and of adult non communicable diseases.
maternal and child malnutrition is a cause of at least 3*1 child deaths annually and is an important cause of morbidity in mothers and children.
maternal undernutrition and childhood undernutrition are important problems in low income and lower middle income countries, and maternal overweight is a growing problem in these countries.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and implementation of interventions that reduce maternal and child undernutrition, prevent overweight and obesity in women of reproductive and in children, and thereby improve the nutritional status and health of mothers and children.

the development of new and improved methods to assess maternal and childhood undernutrition and overweight, to quantify the disease burden of these conditions, and to identify and evaluate interventions to improve maternal and child nutrition.
the development, evaluation and implementation of interventions that can reduce the burden of maternal and child malnutrition and its consequences in low income and low and middle income countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

malnutrition in women, children, and adolescents is a cause of a substantial proportion of deaths and disease worldwide, and that interventions to prevent and treat malnutrition in these groups are needed to improve health outcomes.
the burden of malnutrition is high in low income and some middle income countries and is a major contributor to mortality, morbidity, and impaired development.
maternal undernutrition is a major contributor to child deaths and stunted growth, and that overweight is a growing problem in low income and in middle income countries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
malnutrition is the underlying cause of 45% of deaths in children younger than 2 years and is a cause of morbidity and disability for children and women of reproductive age.
the global burden of maternal and child undernutrition is still very high in the developing world and is a major cause of mortality and morbidity.
malnutrition in all its forms remains a major contributor to child and maternal morbidity and mortality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the burden of maternal and child undernutrition is high and is not declining fast enough to reach the Millennium Development Goal targets.
the burden of maternal and child undernutrition is large, is not confined to a small group of low income countries, and is a cause of a substantial proportion of child deaths.
undernutrition is still a major public health problem in low income and some middle income countries, especially for women of reproductive age and children.
